newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- flat, looking to supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- flat, looking to supply.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were flat to a bit softer in early trade on Tuesday as the market looked ahead to a surge in new municipal sales as well as the Treasury's three-year auction, which was weighing on prices.

"We haven't seen any trades, we might be unchanged to down an eighth of a point in spots," a trader said. Though it still was early in the session, traders said few if any bid wanted lists were being circulated.

Municipal bond sales, which this week were expected to rise to nearly $4.1 billion, the second biggest level seen this year, on Tuesday should add up to $1.7 billion in 44 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $1.5 billion in 20 sales, with a $486 million San Antonio, Texas, deal through PaineWebber Inc. topping the list.
On the competitive side, 24 sales totaling $194 million were scheduled. A $53 million Hamilton County, Tenn., deal at 1100 EDT was the largest.
Maine Municipal Bond Bank's $32 million isse was priced at 5.75 percent in 2017 by PaineWebber.

After last week's big rally, traders said that demand remained concentrated in the intermediate sector, as it appeared to represent the best bargains. "There are people who have money to put to work, especially in intermediates," a trader said.
Another said buyers have displayed a preference for this part of the yield curve for the past three months or so, as some fear the long-end still is too risky.
Treasury bonds eased, partly due to concerns about Wall Street's ability to absorb the $17 billion auction of three-year notes this afternoon, and $12 billion of 10-year notes on Wednesday.
In debt futures, the June Treasury bonds fell eight ticks to 109-25/32, while the June municipal bond lost six ticks to 114-30/32. This left the MOB spread at plus 165 ticks.
A gauge of secondary supply, the Standard and Poor's Corp Blue List slipped to $953 million, a level considered fairly lean.
In the secondary market, bids for Delaware River Port Authority of Pennsylvania and New Jersey Revenues of January 1026, which pay a 5-1/2 percent coupon, rose one basis point to 5.75 percent, NET.
And Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, JFK International Air Terminal bonds of December 2022, which pay a 5.75 percent coupon, were unchanged, bid at 5.94 percent, NET.
